starter.title: Starter: chest CT with RT contours, chest radiograph, prostate MRI zones
starter.description: Small committed pack so the app works from a clean clone: one thoracic radiotherapy-planning CT with RTSTRUCT organ-at-risk contours (lungs, heart, esophagus, spinal cord), one portable chest radiograph (CR, MONOCHROME1 rendering fixture) with the same patient's CT localizer, and one axial T2-weighted prostate MRI with manual zonal segmentation (DICOM SEG). Three different patients from three TCIA collections; no cross-collection links.

subjects.why: Compared RTSTRUCT extents of 12 LCTSC subjects: this one has complete organ-at-risk coverage (heart ~99 mm, lungs ~222-231 mm, esophagus ~183 mm craniocaudal) and the CT extends ~87 mm above the lung apices, so the superior mediastinum and thoracic inlet are included. 3 mm slices, B30f kernel, 131 images (smaller than most).

series.roleNoteExtra: Thoracic radiotherapy planning CT from LCTSC (the collection describes average-4DCT or free-breathing planning CTs depending on institution); not a contrast-enhanced diagnostic chest CT.
series.why: Primary axial volume for anatomy navigation and the RT contour targets.

series.teachingNote: Radiotherapy organ-at-risk contours used clinically for treatment planning and reviewed/edited for consistency with the RTOG 1106 contouring atlas (LCTSC collection description). They are RT planning definitions, not necessarily anatomical teaching boundaries: the cranio-caudal start/stop levels and in-plane conventions (e.g. what is included with the heart, esophagus or cord) follow the RT atlas.
series.why: Source-manual reference contours for lungs, heart, esophagus and spinal cord.

subjects.why: Frontal portable chest radiograph stored as CR with PhotometricInterpretation MONOCHROME1 (needed as an inversion rendering fixture). The same patient has a CT PE study one day later (shifted dates); its 1-image CT 'locator' is included as a role-'scout' fixture showing that a CT localizer is not a chest radiograph.

series.note: CR, XR CHEST AP PORTABLE, MONOCHROME1
series.roleNote: Diagnostic frontal chest radiograph (CR, study 'XR CHEST AP PORTABLE'; ViewPosition empty in the header, AP per study description; burned-in 'Portable UPRIGHT' and side marker).
series.why: MONOCHROME1 fixture kept byte-for-byte in its original transfer syntax.
Scout fixture + uncompressed CT transfer syntax in the committed pack.

subjects.why: Has both the axial T2 TSE series and a 'PROSTATEx Zone Segmentations' SEG (4 manual segments: peripheral zone, transition zone, prostatic urethra, anterior fibromuscular stroma) on the same 384x384 grid; small (19 slices).

series.why: Axial T2-weighted prostate MRI; stored as JPEG 2000 lossless to exercise that decoder.

series.teachingNote: Manual zonal segmentation from the 'PROSTATEx Zone Segmentations' analysis result (Meyer et al. 2020), drawn on this axial T2-weighted series by one annotator (SEG ContentCreatorName 'Reader1'). Zonal boundaries on T2 MRI involve interpretation; treat these outlines as one expert-derived reference, not absolute truth.
series.why: Source-manual zonal anatomy targets (DICOM SEG -> image_px contours).

body.title: Body: kidney tumour CT, contrast chest CT, more thoracic RT cases
body.description: Arterial-phase abdominal CT with kidney and kidney-tumour segmentation (C4KC-KiTS, DICOM SEG); an IV-contrast chest CT whose range covers the whole superior mediastinum and thoracic inlet (great-vessel navigation; no reference targets); and two more LCTSC thoracic planning CTs from different institutions with RT organ-at-risk contours, for unseen-patient practice. Four different patients; the KiTS CT is stored RLE-lossless as a decoder fixture.

subjects.why: Probed slice thickness of the 14 smallest KiTS arterial series via getSingleImage: KiTS-00015 is 3 mm (75 images) with ContrastBolusAgent 'OMNIPAQUE 350' recorded; the SEG (Kidney, Mass) is defined on this arterial series.

series.why: Arterial (corticomedullary) phase CT; stored as RLE lossless to exercise that decoder.
series.roleNoteExtra: Arterial phase of a three-phase CT (KiTS19: segmentations correspond to the arterial phase).

series.teachingNote: KiTS19 kidney and tumour segmentation (C4KC-KiTS). Per the collection description, segmentations were performed by students under the supervision of an experienced urologic cancer surgeon on the arterial phase; the DICOM SEG records SegmentAlgorithmType SEMIAUTOMATIC. 'Kidney' covers both kidneys; see provenanceDetail.note for whether it overlaps the 'Mass' segment. Pathology is not part of this target.

subjects.why: Contrast chest CT for a 'five great vessels' navigation exercise: study 'CT CHEST W CONTRAST', axial 3 mm series '3X3S' (118 images), ContrastBolusAgent 'CONTRAST' in the header; scan range z -357..-6 mm reaches the lower neck, ~90 mm cranial to the aortic arch (checked visually during curation), so the arch branches and brachiocephalic veins are included. Patient not used in chest-pairs.

series.roleNoteExtra: IV contrast-enhanced chest CT (study 'CT CHEST W CONTRAST'; ContrastBolusAgent 'CONTRAST').

subjects.why: Second LCTSC institution (S2, GE): average-intensity projection of a 4DCT ('Ave-IP(10)'), 144 images; complete OAR set (heart ~88 mm, lungs ~272 mm cranio-caudal).

series.roleNote: Primary axial planning CT of this subject although derived: average-intensity projection over 10 phases of a 4DCT (ImageType DERIVED\SECONDARY\REFORMATTED; SeriesDescription 'Ave-IP(10) 0%..90%'). neuro-msk.title: Neuro and MSK: brain MRI sequences, spine levels, mammogram mass
neuro-msk.description: Pre-operative brain MRI of one glioma patient (3D T1 post-contrast, axial T2 BLADE, axial FLAIR) with tumour, ventricle and cerebrum DICOM SEGs (ReMIND); one spine CT with vertebral-level segmentation T1-L5 for level identification (Spine-Mets-CT-SEG); one CBIS-DDSM craniocaudal film-screen mammogram with the source ROI mask and source-stated pathology.

subjects.why: Ranked ReMIND pre-op subjects by tumour-SEG size among those with FLAIR: ReMIND-025 has T1 post-contrast, T2 BLADE and FLAIR plus tumour, ventricle and cerebrum SEGs, and is small (57.6 MB raw). Only the Preop study is used (no intra-operative MR/US).

series.teachingNote: ReMIND pre-operative segmentation defined on the 3D T1 post-contrast series (frames resampled/cropped by the source and mapped back to the T1 slices through patient coordinates). more-ct-xr.title: More CT and X-ray: pediatric organ atlas, RICORD radiographs, more chest pairs
more-ct-xr.description: 21 patients not used in any other pack: four pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis / abdomen-pelvis CTs (ages 1-15 y) with expert contours of up to 29 structures (atlas layer); six COVID-19-positive adult chest radiographs (MIDRC-RICORD-1C) with per-reader study-level labels; four COVID-19-AR same-day radiograph + axial CT pairs; four LIDC-IDRI nodule CTs with multi-reader outlines plus radiographs (interval unknown); three more LCTSC thoracic planning CTs with RT organ-at-risk contours.

subjects.why: Screened 36 Pediatric-CT-SEG subjects (age, coverage, ROI extents, slice thickness via getSingleImage). 1-year-old boy (PatientAge 001Y), chest-abdomen-pelvis CT (lungs fully contoured ~116-122 mm; thymus contoured), GE, 'PO & IV CONTRAST', 182 images at 2 mm.

series.why: Pediatric CT with expert organ contours.
series.roleNoteExtra: Pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis or abdomen-pelvis CT (Pediatric-CT-SEG). SliceThickness 2 mm; per the collection description most datasets were reformatted from 0.6/0.625 mm to 2.0 mm by cubic-spline interpolation before contouring (most superior/inferior slices may show interpolation artifacts).

series.teachingNote: Expert organ contours from Pediatric-CT-SEG, made for patient-specific CT organ-dose estimation (collection: 'expert contours of up to twenty-nine structures'). Most datasets were contoured on CT reformatted to 2.0 mm by cubic-spline interpolation, which can cause artifacts in the most superior/inferior slices (collection description). 'Skin' is the body outline and 'Bones' one structure for all bones; definitions follow the dosimetry project, not a teaching atlas. Atlas layer: for exploration, not authoritative grading.
